# Research

::: {.lede}
Fertility and family demography in Norway: economic uncertainty, childlessness, social parenting, and gender.
:::

Two questions run through my work. First, how do objective and subjective economic uncertainty, from unemployment to pessimistic expectations about the future, affect whether people want children and whether they actually have them? Second, as more people separate and form new partnerships, what does living with a partner's children mean for one's own fertility and for who ends up childless? The short answer from the dissertation: perceived insecurity lowers fertility independently of actual income and employment, and a growing share of "childless" men are in fact raising children as social fathers.

## Data and methods

Norwegian administrative register data (individual, municipal and national level), the Generations and Gender Survey (GGS 2020/2024), panel and event-history methods. Analyses in R and Stata.
